messages:
alex: hitting sustained apiserver 5xx spikes in eu-west1 starting ~10:02 UTC. Grafana shows watch backoff and keepalive resets coinciding with a flurry of GPU attach retries from the provisioner.

jordan: saw controller-manager queue depth climb ~10:05, a few controllers falling behind. not seeing cpu pressure on controlplane nodes though.

maya: quick logs from apiserver-0:```
E03 21 10:02:12 apiserver.go:120] watch connection closed: read tcp 10.2.0.5:443->10.3.1.9:52344: read: connection reset by peer
E03 21 10:02:13 etcdclient: clientv3: deadline exceeded
W03 21 10:03:00 authentication: token validation error: upstream timeout
```

lina: provisioner events are noisy: attaching RTX pods -> attach timeout -> detach -> requeue. Looks like a burst of attach requests from a single job in eu-west1-prod-gpu. job id: batch/encoder-7789.

oncall-sre: pinging network team, also verifying NAT/conntrack exhaustion on the node pool. can someone share node-level conntrack counts and kube-proxy logs? @deploy-bot can you dump the last 200 kube-proxy logs from one of the controlplane nodes? :mag:

deploy-bot: kube-proxy logs attached (excerpt):```
Mar 21 10:02:11 kube-proxy[1972]: conntrack: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
Mar 21 10:02:11 kube-proxy[1972]: failed to sync endpoints: write tcp 10.2.0.5:8443->10.4.2.12:52321: write: connection reset by peer
```

jordan: conntrack table full would explain keepalive resets and watch churn. If attach storms are driving ephemeral connection count high, it cascades to apiserver watch drops and etcd client deadlines.

maya: quick mitigation idea: add a temporary NAT/conntrack harbor (bigger table) or move heavy attach traffic to a different AZ regionally. Also can we throttle batch/encoder job to flatten attach rate?

lina: I can patch the job to add --concurrency=4 and restart controllers feeding it. quick win.

oncall-sre: doing a rolling restart of kube-proxy on a sample controlplane node to free conntrack entries and increasing net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to 200k on controlplane nodes as emergency. will monitor.

alex: agree on throttling the job and conntrack bump. long-term we should tune provisioner backoff + batching to avoid per-pod attach fanout hitting NAT limits. this is an ops+infra doc item.

oncall-sre: monitoring dashboards show 5xx rate falling after kube-proxy restart and conntrack bump. keeping this thread updated. next: follow-up RCA and a cost/availability discussion on whether to add reserved NAT capacity for eu-west1 GPU pools.

jordan: note for cost tradeoff: reserved NAT increases bill but prevents these cascades; alternate is smarter provisioner batching (software) which is cheaper but takes engineering cycles.

maya: created a short runbook patch:
- throttle batch encoder to 4 concurrent attach jobs
- bump nf_conntrack_max on controlplane nodes to 200k
- restart kube-proxy on 2/3 controlplane nodes sequentially
- monitor apiserver 5xx and controller queue depth for 15m

lina: applied throttle and restart on encoder job, will report in 5m.

oncall-sre: marking incident socket:linked and will open postmortem if 5xx > threshold for 30m. good coordination, thanks. :thumbsup:
